subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 2026.6.11 fails codesign/spctl despite valid DMG checksum

question: Should OpenClaw reissue the v2026.6.11 macOS DMG/zip after live Apple Silicon signature verification, or leave remediation for a later stable release with explicit user guidance?
rationale: Only release/security maintainers can access the restricted macOS signing lane and decide whether replacing a stable artifact is safer than deferring to the next release.

options.title: Verify and reissue macOS assets
options.body: Run the restricted macOS validation/publish path and replace the affected stable assets only after copied-app `codesign` and `spctl` proof passes.

options.title: Defer with release guidance
options.body: Keep the issue open and tell users to wait for the next stable macOS artifact if same-version replacement is too risky.

options.title: Close after artifact proof
options.body: Close only if maintainers prove the current or already-rebuilt asset passes the exact reported verification path.

recommendation.title: Verify and reissue macOS assets
recommendation.body: Run the restricted macOS validation/publish path and replace the affected stable assets only after copied-app `codesign` and `spctl` proof passes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and release-signing workflow history point to this handle as the best available routing candidate.
